name: math_tensor_product

phase_0.boundary_condition: The universal property of the tensor product

VINIT.justification: The initial state before the construction of the free vector space over the Cartesian product.

TANCH.chosen_element: The tensor product space V ⊗ W
TANCH.justification: The terminal object in the category of bilinear maps from V × W.

AFWD.chosen_element: Canonical injection into the free space
AFWD.justification: The forward mapping of pairs (v, w) to formal basis elements.

AREV.justification: The descent from the large free space to the specific equivalence classes defining multilinearity.

CLINK.justification: The chaining of maps required to satisfy the universal property diagram.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-recognition of the tensor space as a unique object up to isomorphism.

FSPLIT.justification: The splitting of a single tensor into a sum of basis components across the two constituent spaces.

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the tensor from its distributed components via the summation of the bilinear map.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative state where basis elements remain distinct and non-zero.

EVALF.justification: The negative state where elements are identified with the additive identity through quotienting.

ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous holding of multiple possible decompositions for the same tensor.

IFIX.justification: The permanent, invariant rank of the resulting space which cannot be altered.

phase_3.void_description: The null space before vector space definition
phase_3.false_description: The zero element of the tensor space
phase_3.both_description: An unreduced formal sum of pairs

steps.domain_action: Initialize the empty set for the construction of the product domain
Map the Cartesian product V × W into the formal free vector space F(V × W)
Record the initial formal basis elements as permanent entries
Branch the formal sum into individual scalar-vector pairs for multilinearity testing
Validate the additive property (v1 + v2) ⊗ w = v1 ⊗ w + v2 ⊗ w
Recombine the validated relations into the quotient space structure
Compose the quotient map with the free space injection
Verify the uniqueness of the map via the universal property
Hold the tensor in its unreduced and reduced forms simultaneously during calculation
Apply the relations to reduce the formal sum to its simplest tensor form
Fix the final dimension and rank of the tensor product space
Close the system within the boundary of the universal property

phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The tensor product symbol ⊗ acting as a connector
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The basis set of the constituent vector spaces
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The order of operations in the quotienting process

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational overhead of quotient space reduction
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Two independent vector spaces V and W
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A single unified tensor product space V ⊗ W
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information content is conserved through the isomorphism of the universal property.
